title: Types of Script Errors knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Types of Script Errors”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Syntax errors” under lesson 118, “Types of Script Errors”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Types of Script Errors”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics.
questions.explanation: Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Types of Script Errors”?
options: Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output.
questions.explanation: Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
